title: PepsiCo's Snack Portfolio: What's Driving Volume Gains?
author: Na
description: PepsiCo reported improving momentum in its snack portfolio during Q2 2026, with global convenient foods organic volume rising 3% and international volume up 4%. The company gained market share in U.S. salty snacks for a third consecutive quarter, driven by portfolio innovation including portion-control multipacks and healthier permissible offerings. Competitors Mondelez and Hershey are also showing strength through brand innovation and emerging market expansion, though PepsiCo's stock has underperformed its industry peers over the past three months.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong organic volume growth (3% global, 4% international), three consecutive quarters of U.S. salty snack volume growth, market share gains across multiple categories, and successful portfolio diversification with portion-control and healthier product lines. However, stock has underperformed industry by 7.1% in past three months and trades at discount valuation (15.54X vs 19.41X industry average).

Gaining traction with strong Q2 2026 volume, positive volume mix and share gains in North America, successful brand portfolio (Ritz, Oreo, Tate's, Hu), and innovation in protein, gluten-free, and zero-sugar offerings supporting momentum.

Snack portfolio gaining momentum with strong consumer demand for brands like Dot's Pretzels, SkinnyPop, and LesserEvil. Supply-chain constraints resolved and automation improvements supporting volume growth potential.

title: Hershey's Pricing Holds Firm: Can Volume Pressure Ease From Here?
author: Na
description: The Hershey Company reported Q2 2026 organic sales growth of 3.6%, driven by 12% net price realization, but faced an 8% volume decline due to consumer elasticity and value-seeking behavior. The company expects improved core-item availability and increased demand-creation activities to support second-half performance. HSY trades at a forward P/E of 18.71, above industry average, with consensus estimates implying 34.6% and 16.1% year-over-year EPS growth for current and next fiscal years.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Hershey demonstrated pricing strength with 12% net price realization and positive organic sales growth of 3.6%, this was significantly offset by an 8% volume decline due to consumer elasticity. The company holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating and trades above industry valuation multiples. The outlook depends on whether improved availability and demand creation can offset continued elasticity pressures.

title: Cocoa Prices are Falling: Should You Buy Hershey's Stock?
author: Parkev Tatevosian, Cfa
description: With cocoa prices declining, investors are questioning whether Hershey stock presents a buying opportunity. The article examines how falling commodity costs could impact the chocolate manufacturer's operations and stock performance, noting that the business has experienced unusual volatility.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents a balanced inquiry into whether falling cocoa prices benefit Hershey stock, without making a definitive recommendation. The mention of unusual business volatility and the questioning tone suggest caution, but the potential cost savings from lower cocoa prices could be positive. The neutral stance reflects the complexity of the situation.

title: 1 Stat That Makes Hershey Stock Hard to Ignore Heading Into Fall
author: Catie Hogan
description: Hershey demonstrates strong pricing power despite cocoa costs surging over 120% in six months. Q2 earnings showed 6.6% net sales growth and 57% adjusted EPS growth, indicating successful price increases without losing customers. With 82% of parents planning to buy chocolate in October, Hershey's expanded 'Hersheyween' promotion positions it well for the season. The stock offers a 3.2% dividend yield and is trading below its 52-week high, making it attractive for income-focused investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Hershey demonstrates exceptional pricing power with 57% EPS growth despite 120%+ cocoa cost increases, indicating strong brand strength and consumer demand. The company's expanded Halloween promotions and 3.2% dividend yield position it well for seasonal demand. Stock trades below 52-week highs, offering value for income investors.

title: Elon Musk Owns 48.4% of SpaceX, a New Filing Shows. Here's Why That Matters for Everyone Else Holding the Stock.
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: A new SEC filing reveals that Elon Musk controls 48.4% of SpaceX's voting power, giving him effective control over major company decisions including mergers, acquisitions, and capital investments. The article compares this to The Hershey Foundation's 80% control of Hershey, noting that SpaceX investors are essentially investing alongside Musk. Whether this concentration of power is positive or negative depends on investor confidence in Musk's leadership.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article presents Musk's 48.4% stake as a double-edged sword—neither inherently positive nor negative. It depends on investor perspective: those who trust Musk's vision may view it positively, while those concerned about concentrated power may view it negatively. The article takes a balanced, informational stance without advocating for either position.

Hershey is used as a comparative example to illustrate governance structures and shareholder dynamics. The article notes the foundation's control prevents takeovers, which may or may not benefit shareholders. No specific investment recommendation or sentiment is expressed about Hershey itself.
